value.0: Vital Rupture isn't a lesson between us anymore. You proved it in the Veles Militia Annex. Keep your hands steady when nobody's grading it.
Your grip's still learning what it's holding. I don't teach Vital Rupture to hands that haven't finished learning the knife itself. Come back when the vibroknife stops surprising you.

Your grip rides high on the hilt - that's a throat angle, not mine. I want to see if it can be taught out of you. Adepts are drilling Vital Rupture wrong in the Veles Militia Annex on Viscara, six of them, sloppy work all of it. Kill them, bring me back their drill ledger, and we'll see what you have.
Then go. The annex key is already on you; it opens the sealed gate. Cut clean, or don't cut at all.

I patched enough arterial wounds to know exactly where they open. Teaching someone to open them on purpose is the same knowledge, aimed the other direction. I'd rather you learn it from me than from a corpse's mistake.
The Veles Militia Annex sits off the main garrison road on Viscara. The gate is sealed; the key I gave you opens it. Follow the access route in and stay inside the annex proper.
The adepts in there are quick studies with dull technique. Six of them, practicing on each other and on anyone who wanders in. Don't get flattered by an easy first cut - the second one won't be.
The adepts are still standing in the Veles Militia Annex. Come back when six of them aren't.
You found it. Hand over the drill ledger and let me see what state their handwriting is in.
Handwriting's shaky, technique worse. Six down is a start, not a proof. Word finds me when you're ready for the second lesson.

Pulse still even. Good, fear ruins the cut before the blade does. The annex has specialists now, five of them, refining what the adepts botched. Drop them, and bring me the range relay they've been logging kills on.
Go. The annex gate still knows your key. This time, don't stop at good enough.

A rupture cut opens the femoral or the brachial and lets pressure do the rest. Done right, it's over before they understand what happened. Done sloppy, and this annex is full of sloppy, you get someone who bleeds for ten minutes screaming instead of ten seconds quiet. That's cruelty pretending to be skill.
Same annex, same gate, deeper in. The specialists have claimed the training floor past the first checkpoint. Your key still opens the way; it doesn't open sympathy.
Five specialists who've had the adepts' mistakes beaten out of them. They'll test your guard before your grip. Don't rush the count - dead is dead whether you took your time or not.
Five specialists, still breathing, still in the annex. Go finish the count.
The relay's in your hand. Let's see what it logged.
Kill counts, mostly theirs, some inflated. You're past adept work now. The annex still has a warden who thinks rank protects him from you.

The warden runs live drills on students who can't say no. He's earned the title by outliving whoever the annex sent at him solo. I'm not sending you in solo either. Find two people whose blade you'd trust at your own throat, then take his scored challenge badge off him.
Then arrange your company and go. The gate still answers to your key.

Every one of these students learned the cut from someone who learned it from someone who never treated a wound in his life. It shows in how they hold the blade, like it's a threat and not a tool. The warden trained half of them personally. That should tell you what his lesson looks like.
Deeper still, past the specialists' floor, behind a locked partition the annex calls the arena. Your key clears the outer gate; the warden's door opens because you'll put it in.
He has opened quicker hands than yours, and he did it alone against people who came alone. Don't. Bring the two you trust, or don't bring yourself.
The warden is still holding his floor. Bring your company and go end that.
You're still standing, and so's the badge. Hand it over.
Scored, cracked down the middle. He'll heal wrong and remember why. You've done what most of his students couldn't. There's an inner circle above him who won't like that.

The inner circle runs what's left of the warden's operation, four instructors who liked their rank more than their students. Clean margins means nothing left ragged when you're done. Take their captain's challenge chit off whichever of them is still holding it when the others are down.
Go settle it. You've earned enough trust here that I won't ask twice.

The ledger told me who was still sloppy. The relay told me who was logging kills to pad a report. The badge told me the warden finally lost to someone who deserved it. Bring me their chit and I'll tell you what it says about the four of them.
They've sealed the command floor above the arena. The same key that got you this far still turns in that lock; they never thought anyone would get this far to use it.
Four of them, and they fight like people who've never had to fight alone. Neither should you. Bring backup, or count on being outnumbered the whole way through.
Four of the inner circle, still upright. Go make that untrue.
That's the chit. Let me read what they signed.
Four names, four confessions dressed as duty logs. The annex answers to me again below this floor. Only the master's left, and he taught the warden everything the warden got wrong trying to copy.

The master doesn't drill students. He performs on them, once, and once is always enough. He's the reason Vital Rupture works at all, and the reason it can kill the person doing it. No one goes to him alone and walks back out to tell me about it. Take people you'd trust to close a wound of yours. When he's down, that's the only proof I need.
Then go end it properly. You won't need the key explained to you again.

One rule, and it's the only one that's mattered from the first cut to this one: don't enjoy it. The moment the bleed stops being technique and starts being pleasure, you've become one of his students instead of mine.
Past everything you've already cleared, at the annex's deepest floor, the one the inner circle kept locked even from their own instructors. You've earned every door between here and there.
He taught the rupture cut before the warden ever held a knife. No one who went in solo came out to correct that record. Bring the people you'd bleed for, because down there, you might.
The master is still down there, still breathing on his own schedule. Go change that.
He's down, and you're upright. That's rarer than you'd think.
Terminal bleed, textbook placement, yours, not his, for once. Vital Rupture is yours now, the same way it was mine: earned, not performed. Don't let me hear that you're enjoying it.
Back to the ledger.
I'll take the first cut.
Why does a medic teach killing?
Where do I find the annex?
What should I expect from the adepts?
Not yet.
Here's the drill ledger.
Back to the relay.
I'll map the second one.
What exactly is a rupture cut?
Where are the specialists training?
What should I expect this time?
I need more time.
Here's the range relay.
Back to the badge.
I'll bring my two and go.
What's wrong with how these students fight?
Where's the warden's floor?
What should I know about him?
Not with strangers at my back.
Here's the badge - he's done.
Back to the chit.
I'll clean the circle out.
What do these proofs tell you?
Where's the inner circle hiding?
What am I walking into?
Give me a day to find my two.
Here's the chit.
Back to it.
I'll bring who I trust. Let's finish this.
Is there a rule I should know?
Where do I find him?
What should I expect from the master?
I need to be sure of my company first.
It's done. He's finished.
